descriptionChirho: Qal: to pass on, pass through, or sweep by a location in physical movement. Used of a spirit passing by (Job 4:15), God passing by unseen (Job 9:11, 11:10), reed-boats sweeping past (Job 9:26), the Assyrian sweeping through Judah (Isa 8:8, 21:1), wind sweeping by (Hab 1:11), and Samuel's instruction to Saul to 'pass on ahead' (1 Sam 10:3). Multilingual glosses: arb marrat/ta'buru, hin guzri/guzrega, kor jinagada, spa pasara/pasa.

Qal: to pass away, vanish, cease to exist, conveying transience and ephemerality. Grass that sprouts and then passes away (Ps 90:5-6), heavens that will pass away like a garment (Ps 102:26), the glory of nations that shall pass away (Isa 2:18), the winter rain that 'is over and gone' (Song 2:11). Multilingual evidence: arb yataghyyaru/tazulu, hin badal jata hai, kor sarajirira, spa pasaran/desapareceran.

Hifil/Piel: to change, exchange, or replace one thing for another, especially garments or wages. Laban changed Jacob's wages ten times (Gen 31:7,41), Jacob commands his household to change their garments (Gen 35:2), Joseph changed his garments before Pharaoh (Gen 41:14; cf. 2 Sam 12:20), exchanging a dedicated animal for another (Lev 27:10), replacing cut cedars with new ones (Isa 9:10), and God changing the heavens like a garment (Ps 102:26). Glosses: arb ghayyara, deu geandert/wechselte, hin badli/badle, kor bakkuuda, spa cambio/cambiarás.

Hifil: to renew strength or vitality, or of a plant producing fresh growth after being cut down. A tree cut down whose stump will sprout again (Job 14:7), an eagle renewing its youth (Job 29:20), those who wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength (Isa 40:31), and the coastlands called to renew their arguments (Isa 41:1). Multilingual glosses: arb yujaddiduna/tatajaddadu, hin naye karenge, kor saeropge harira, spa renovaran/retonará.

Qal: to violate or transgress a covenant or ordinance, figuratively 'passing over' or disregarding what is binding. Used in Isaiah 24:5 where the inhabitants of the earth have 'violated the statutes' and broken the everlasting covenant. Glosses: arb ghayyaru, hin badla, kor bakkuossni, spa violaron.

Qal: to pierce through or penetrate, of a weapon or sharp object passing through the body. Jael drove the tent peg through Sisera's temple so that it 'pierced through' (Judg 5:26), and the arrow that pierces through a man's body (Job 20:24). Multilingual glosses: arb thaqabat/takhtariquhu, hin chheda/bhedega, kor gwantonghaeda/kkwollirira, spa atraveso/lo traspasara.
